title: Lowest Common Ancestor of a Binary Search Tree
description: Given a binary search tree and two nodes p and q in it, return their lowest common ancestor: the deepest node that has both p and q as descendants (a node can be its own descendant).

reference.use_case: Finding the most specific shared parent of two items in a hierarchy, such as the closest common folder, manager, or version two items descend from.
system_examples: Git — git merge-base finds the best common ancestor of two commits to drive three-way merges
Org-chart and file-permission systems — the lowest folder or manager that contains both members determines shared access
IP routing — the longest common prefix of two addresses identifies the smallest subnet containing both
reference.explanation: In a BST the ordering tells you where to go: if both values are smaller go left, if both are larger go right, otherwise the current node is the split point, giving O(h) time and O(1) space. General trees and DAGs (like Git history) need heavier methods, but the idea of locating where two paths diverge is the same.
